title: Bosonic Matsubara partial fractions of coth
latent_structure: Infinite sum over bosonic Matsubara poles n*pi*I of the simple-pole kernel 2z/(z^2 + n^2 pi^2) plus the n=0 term 1/z equals coth z. Equivalent compact form Sum_{n=-oo..oo} 1/(n^2 + q^2) = pi coth(pi q)/q with z = pi q. Closed special function vs spectral sum of poles.

function_domains.coth: poles at z = n*pi*I, n in Z (DLMF 4.36 preamble)
function_domains.sinh: zeros at n*pi*I, n in Z

nonzero_conditions.statement: z != n*pi*I for all integers n
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: DLMF 4.36: 'When z ≠ n π i, n ∈ ℤ' immediately before 4.36.3–4.36.5

analytic_domains.statement: z not an integer multiple of pi*I
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED

branch_conventions: coth z = cosh(z)/sinh(z); principal entire sinh, cosh

derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: sinh zeros are exactly z = n*pi*I

why_not_cse_lgg: The compact side is a single hyperbolic function; the expanded side is an infinite sum of rational poles. CSE cannot sum the family. This is the bosonic Matsubara frequency sum, a special-function representation.
proposer_leak_risk: Do not leak 'Matsubara', 'Bose distribution', or the equivalent pi*coth(pi*q)/q form as a gold name. Source writes coth and the sum.
notes: coth not in PARSE_POLICY: use cosh/sinh. Sibling 4.36.4 is csch(z)**2 = Sum 1/(z - n*pi*I)**2 on the same pole set (trigamma-like bosonic kernel). Thermal reading T>0 / beta>0 is NOT imported: the source is a complex-function identity with explicit pole exclusion.
